payloads.name: ps5-dualsense-overlay
payloads.author: erickdavestech
payloads.release_notes:
On-screen **DualSense controller overlay** for a PS5 running homebrew. Load it once per boot, open any game, and the controller appears bottom-left, lighting up in real time.

## Download

`ps5-dualsense-overlay-v1.0.1.elf` — SHA-256 in `SHA256SUMS.txt`:

```text
3790c590088b275a8d803c7c46394af6c7e0d8ede2546c0507a05a246fbf9747  ps5-dualsense-overlay-v1.0.1.elf
```

## What's Changed in v1.0.1

### Fixed
- **Overlay freeze after Rest Mode (sleep/resume):** Fixed issue where `sceUserServiceGetForegroundUser` returning `0xffffffff` (-1) during console standby or before logging into an account caused pad initialization to permanently fail, leaving the overlay visible on screen but completely frozen.
- **Controller disconnect / standby recovery:** If `scePadReadState` fails continuously for 15 consecutive frames (e.g. controller turned off, Bluetooth drop, or system suspend), the dead handle is now safely closed via `scePadClose` and re-acquired automatically as soon as the controller is back online.

### Added
- **Periodic foreground user detection:** The overlay now checks for foreground user account switches every ~2 seconds and re-binds the pad handle when switching local accounts.
- **Non-blocking pad initialization retry:** Periodic retry every 30 frames (~0.5s) if user or handle was not immediately ready at startup.

## Usage

1. Jailbreak the console as usual (tested with kstuff-lite).
2. Load `ps5-dualsense-overlay-v1.0.1.elf` with your payload manager, in either of these ways:
   - **Web portal:** from a PC or phone on the same network, open the payload manager's portal using the console's local IP and upload the `.elf`.
   - **USB:** copy the `.elf` to a USB drive, connect it to the console and launch it from the payload manager.
3. Open any game.

Load it only **once** per boot, and do not run it together with Common FPS or SimpleFPS: they inject into the same system process. To update, reboot and load the new version.

payloads.author: Swordpdf
payloads.release_notes:
**PS5SX2 2.10** (build vk-285-171)

**New**
- **PS2 discs on the PS5 home screen.** Put a PS2 DVD in the console's drive while you are on the home screen: a tile with the game's name and cover shows up in about 6 seconds, and the PS5's own "Unsupported Disc" tile is hidden. Press **✕** on it and the game starts straight from the disc (or from its copy in `games/`, if you made one): no shelf, no question. Take the disc out and the tile goes away.
- **A "Reload PS2 Disc" tile.** If a disc's tile does not come, does not start, or the "Unsupported Disc" tile stays: press this tile once. It cleans up after the last game, has ShadowMount+ look again and makes the disc's tile again. A pop-up says "PS2 disc reloaded." a few seconds later.
- **A question on the shelf.** With PS5SX2 open, a PS2 disc that is not copied yet asks **Play from disc** or **Copy to storage** (**Left / Right** choose, **✕** confirms, **○** is "not now"). *Play from disc* starts at once and reads the disc as you play, like a real PS2, so the disc has to stay in. *Copy to storage* copies it first (several minutes) and plays from the copy: faster loading, and the disc can come out. A disc that `games/` already holds starts from its copy with no question. So you can still dump a disc through the shelf, and once it is dumped, starting its game from the tile runs the dump instead of the disc.

**Changed**
- A PS2 disc put in on the home screen no longer starts PS5SX2 by itself: press its tile.
- The empty file `nodiscask` in `/data/PCSX2/flags/` brings the 2.03 behaviour back: no question on the shelf, and a disc put in on the home screen is copied and started by itself. Use it if you don't use ShadowMount+, because the tiles need it.

payloads.name: librespot-ps5
payloads.author: stupiditytries
payloads.release_notes:
First release. Spotify Connect on a modified PS5, playing over your games.

## What you need

- A PS5 that can load ELF payloads
- [klogsrv](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/klogsrv) running on the console
- A USB drive the console plays music from (exFAT or FAT32, not extended storage) with about 8 GB free
- Spotify Premium, and the Spotify app on a phone on the same network as the console

## How to use it

1. Download `librespot-ps5.elf` below, put it on a USB drive and load it with your payload loader.
2. On the console, open the **Music** tab in the control centre.
3. Go to your **external drive**.
4. Open the folder **Start Librespot** and play **Librespot Streamer**.
5. In the Spotify app on your phone, open the device list and pick **PS5 Connect**.

The program makes the folders and tracks itself the first time it runs. If they do not show up in the music list, open any other music folder once and go back.

After you press play on the console there are about 14 seconds of silence before the music starts. After that, everything you do in the Spotify app is heard about two seconds later, and the music keeps playing when you start a game.

To stop, play **Stop Librespot** in the folder **Librespot Controls**, or pause from the phone.

## Known issues

- Track notifications show on the home screen but not yet while a game is in front.
- Pausing from the console costs about 14 seconds of silence when you resume. Pausing from the phone does not.
- Next and Previous on the console do nothing useful; use the phone.
- After 12 hours the stream has to be started again.
- Tested on one console and one USB drive.

How it works, the settings and the build steps are in the [README](https://github.com/stupiditytries/librespot-ps5#readme).

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Spotify or Sony.

payloads.name: pegasus-dl
payloads.author: pegasus-ps5
payloads.release_notes:
- Parallel downloads now use persistent connections and write ranges directly
  into the temporary file, avoiding a final segment-copy pass. New configurations
  default to 16 connections, with a single-stream fallback for incompatible hosts.
- RAR/RAR5 and 7z archive cache downloads use the same parallel engine. Paused
  downloads resume from checked checkpoints, and paused extraction restarts from
  the completed cache without downloading again.
- Completed RAR caches survive password prompts and wrong passwords. UTF-8
  passwords and retries for legacy encrypted RAR files are handled correctly.
- Extraction progress now counts bytes across files. Cancellation and
  finalization are coordinated to avoid committing cancelled work.
- Archive replacement failures restore the previous destination, stored RAR
  entries receive CRC checks, and failed format probes clean up their temporary
  files.

# OnionHEN v0.9.0

OnionHEN is a homebrew enabler and Toolbox for jailbroken PS5 consoles, built on etaHEN. It prepares the system, injects a Toolbox into the home screen, and adds cheats, a game overlay, payload management, and background services.

**Version:** v0.9.0 is the stable release following v0.9.0-beta1 and v0.9.0-beta2. It brings together their changes since [v0.0.13](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/releases/tag/v0.0.13).

## What changed since v0.0.13

### Firmware compatibility

This release adds support for firmware **13.0-13.6** and **some 5.50 consoles**. Reports from real hardware are welcome.

### Cheats

On firmware 4.03, opening the cheats menu for a game with no cheats could take about 40 seconds, then leave the home screen unresponsive until a forced reboot ([#97](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/issues/97), [#103](https://github.com/aydencharles/onionHEN/issues/103)). The beta2 fix makes an empty menu return in a few seconds without stalling ShellUI. The reporter on #103 confirmed the problem was gone in an early beta2 build.

Long cheat names are also truncated on UTF-8 boundaries.

### elfldr

v0.0.13 needed elfldr v0.22 because it loaded the cache through a `file:` URI. v0.9.0 sends a normal ELF to port **9021**, so older elfldr builds work again. An external elfldr must still be listening on 9021.

payloads.name: ps5debug-NG
payloads.author: Pharaoh2k
payloads.release_notes:
# ps5debug-NG v1.3.2

v1.3.0 was the big feature release. **v1.3.2 is the correctness and reliability release** that follows it: writes now prove they landed, three separate session-killing bugs are fixed, a scan comparator that silently returned wrong results is repaired, and firmware support extends through **FW 13.60**.

There was no separate v1.3.1 download, so **this release also contains everything from v1.3.1** (Turbo Scan cancel).

---

### ⚠️ Read this first: writes are now verified, and that changes what you see

Process writes used to report success as soon as the write was handed off. They are now **read back and compared before success is reported**, so a write that silently did nothing now correctly reports a failure.

**If you are a client developer:** a write that previously appeared to succeed may now return `CMD_ERROR`. That is the bug surfacing, not a new bug. Servers advertise **capability level `1.1`** so clients can detect the behaviour.

- `CMD_PROC_WRITE` returns terminal `CMD_ERROR` on write or verification failure.
- Write-multi returns **typed per-entry status codes** (invalid / DMAP / verify / mdbg) so you can tell exactly which entries failed and why, instead of losing the detail in one aggregate result.
- A proven DMAP mismatch no longer quietly falls through to the mdbg path.
- **Caveat:** a transfer whose start address ends in `0xFF` backs up one byte to keep the write aligned. That adjacent-byte read-modify-write is not atomic, so it needs a **stable or suspended target** to be safe.

---

### 🛠️ Session-killing bugs fixed

- **Fixed a debug session wedge that required a console reboot.** Toggling a trainer patch while the target was stopped at a breakpoint could deadlock the sole debug worker: an RPC stop was issued against a process the debugger already held ptrace-stopped, so the wait never returned, the worker died, and every reattach afterwards failed (clients reported "Process not connected" / already-debugging) until the console was restarted.
- **Fixed a crash...

**PS5SX2 2.10** (build vk-285-171)

**New**
- **PS2 discs on the PS5 home screen.** Put a PS2 DVD in the console's drive while you are on the home screen: a tile with the game's name and cover shows up in about 6 seconds, and the PS5's own "Unsupported Disc" tile is hidden. Press **✕** on it and the game starts straight from the disc (or from its copy in `games/`, if you made one): no shelf, no question. Take the disc out and the tile goes away.

A disc that `games/` already holds starts from its copy with no question. So you can still dump a disc through the shelf, and once it is dumped, starting its game from the tile runs the dump instead of the disc.

payloads.description: PS5 Time & Date Sync v1.0.0 by kerrdec97
payloads.author: kerrdec97
payloads.release_notes:
# PS5 Time & Date Sync by Deckerr97

Initial public release.

A standalone, one-shot PS5 payload that restores the console date and time using public NTP servers. It is designed for consoles whose CMOS/RTC battery no longer retains the clock after a complete shutdown.

## Features

- Automatic NTP date and time synchronization
- Published Cloudflare numeric fallbacks when PS5 DNS is unavailable
- Cloudflare, pool.ntp.org, and Google Public NTP hostname fallbacks
- NTP endpoint, version, mode, stratum, request timestamp, and date validation
- Clock read-back verification after updating
- Preserves the configured PS5 timezone
- One notification per payload execution
- No application installation or file modification
- Automatically exits after completion

## Requirements

- Compatible PS5 exploit and ELF payload loader
- Internet access with outbound UDP port 123
- An execution environment that permits `settimeofday`

Built using a PS5 Payload SDK package containing firmware definitions through 13.60. Actual runtime compatibility depends on the firmware, exploit, loader, and available permissions.

## Acknowledgements

Special thanks to **John Törnblom** and every contributor to the [PS5 Payload SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) for creating and maintaining the toolchain that made this payload possible.

## Build verification

- File: `ps5-date-time-sync.elf`
- Size: 130,240 bytes

- Improved SMB package streaming performance, reaching approximately 110 MB/s during installs in ideal conditions
- Added streaming diagnostics to help identify network and server bottlenecks

### Extended USB Storage
- Available-space checks now include extended USB storage (`/mnt/ext0`)

### Package Badges
- PS4 and PS5 package badges are now shown in package lists

### Package Detection and Scanning
- Fixed detection of PS5 DLC packages
- Fixed drive scans hiding other packages when an unknown package was present, such as during a copy operation

---

Full Changelog: https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-pkg-manager/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.1

## Changelog

### Unified Architecture & Upstream Remote Loader Base
* **Single Shared Base**: WebKit Autoloader is now built on top of [ps5-webkit-remote-loader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-remote-loader), unifying the userland exploit runner, ROP primitives, and payload pipeline across both Poops and Relapse.
* **Developer Iteration & Contributions**: Developers looking to experiment with, test, or improve Poops or Relapse can now do so easily in [ps5-webkit-remote-loader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-remote-loader) by loading payloads over the network (port 9027). Any improvements made in that repo can be contributed upstream to directly benefit both projects.

### Dropped umtx2 (FW <= 5.50)
* **Dropped Legacy umtx2 Support**: Support for firmwares 1.00–5.50 via umtx2 has been dropped in this release. That path was not receiving updates and was blocking development and architectural changes.
* **Future Lower Firmware Support**: Support for lower firmwares may be added back in the future if it is added to [ps5-webkit-remote-loader](https://github.com/itsPLK/ps5-webkit-remote-loader). Contributions to bring lower firmware support to the new unified base are welcome!

### Exploit & Stability Improvements
* **Relapse Stability**: Stability and reliability improvements for the Relapse chain.
